events.title: The Asante Empire Rises
events.body: Osei Tutu's Asante defeat their overlords, Denkyira. By tradition the Golden Stool descends from the sky to bind the new nation together.

events.title: The Forty-seven Rōnin
events.body: Forty-seven masterless samurai storm the Edo mansion of the official they blame for their lord's death and kill him. They are ordered to commit ritual suicide, and become heroes of loyalty.

events.title: St Petersburg Founded
events.body: Peter the Great founds a fortress on the marshes of the Neva. It becomes his new capital and Russia's 'window on Europe'.

events.title: The Love Suicides at Sonezaki
events.body: Chikamatsu Monzaemon's puppet play, about a clerk and a courtesan driven to die together, is a sensation in Osaka — drama about ordinary townspeople.

events.title: Opticks
events.body: Isaac Newton publishes his experiments showing that white light is a mixture of colours.

events.title: Kimpa Vita Burned
events.body: Kimpa Vita, a young Kongolese woman who taught that Christ and the saints were African, is burned as a heretic. Her movement had sought to reunite the war-torn Kingdom of Kongo.

events.title: Aurangzeb Dies
events.body: The last great Mughal emperor dies after a long war in the Deccan. The empire, at its largest, begins to break apart.

events.title: Great Britain Is Formed
events.body: England and Scotland unite as the Kingdom of Great Britain, with one parliament at Westminster.

events.title: Mount Fuji Erupts
events.body: Mount Fuji's last eruption begins weeks after a great earthquake, dropping ash on Edo, about 100 kilometres away.

events.title: The Khanate of Kokand
events.body: Around 1709, an Uzbek dynasty breaks away from Bukhara and founds the Khanate of Kokand in the Fergana Valley.

events.title: Iron Smelted With Coke
events.body: Abraham Darby smelts iron with coke instead of charcoal at Coalbrookdale, freeing iron-making from Britain's shrinking forests.

events.title: Poltava
events.body: Peter the Great crushes the army of Charles XII of Sweden. Russia replaces Sweden as the great power of northern Europe.

events.title: The Brazilian Gold Rush
events.body: Gold found in the 1690s draws tens of thousands to Minas Gerais, where Vila Rica — now Ouro Preto — is founded. Enslaved Africans do most of the mining.

events.title: St Paul's Cathedral
events.body: Parliament declares Christopher Wren's new St Paul's complete, 35 years after building began on the ruins left by the Great Fire of London.

events.title: The Newcomen Engine
events.body: Thomas Newcomen's steam engine starts pumping water from a coal mine near Dudley — the first practical steam engine.

events.title: The Treaty of Utrecht
events.body: The War of the Spanish Succession ends. Britain gains Gibraltar and the asiento — the right to supply enslaved Africans to Spain's colonies.

events.title: Smallpox at the Cape
events.body: Smallpox, brought ashore on laundry from a ship, sweeps through Cape Town and the Khoikhoi of the south-western Cape. Their societies never recover.

events.title: The Fall of Barcelona
events.body: After a fourteen-month siege, Barcelona falls to the Bourbon king Philip V, who abolishes Catalonia's own laws and institutions. 11 September is now Catalonia's national day.

events.title: The Kangxi Dictionary
events.body: Scholars working for the Kangxi Emperor complete a dictionary of about 47,000 Chinese characters. Its system of radicals is still used.

events.title: The Cape Chooses Slavery
events.body: The Dutch East India Company's council at the Cape decides to keep relying on enslaved labour rather than bring in European workers. Slavery shapes the colony for over a century.

events.title: The Tulip Period
events.body: After the Peace of Passarowitz, the Ottoman court enters a time of gardens, festivals, poetry and a passion for tulips.

events.title: Robinson Crusoe
events.body: Daniel Defoe publishes the story of a castaway on a Caribbean island, presented as a true account. It is often called the first English novel.

events.title: The Qing in Tibet
events.body: A Qing army drives the Dzungars out of Lhasa and installs a new Dalai Lama, beginning Qing overlordship of Tibet.

events.title: Dutch Learning
events.body: Shogun Yoshimune relaxes the ban on Western books. Japanese scholars begin studying European science and medicine through Dutch traders at Nagasaki.

events.title: Coffee Comes to the Caribbean
events.body: By tradition, the French officer Gabriel de Clieu carries a coffee plant to Martinique around 1720. Coffee plantations worked by enslaved people spread through the Caribbean and Latin America.

events.title: The South Sea Bubble
events.body: Shares in the South Sea Company, which traded enslaved Africans, soar and then crash, ruining investors. Paris suffers a similar collapse the same year.

events.title: The Brandenburg Concertos
events.body: J. S. Bach sends six concertos to the Margrave of Brandenburg. They are not known to have been played there; today they are among the best-loved music of the age.

events.title: Inoculation in Boston
events.body: During a smallpox epidemic, minister Cotton Mather promotes inoculation, which he learned of from Onesimus, an enslaved African man who had been inoculated as a child. Far fewer of the inoculated die.

events.title: Rapa Nui
events.body: On Easter Sunday, Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen reaches Rapa Nui and its giant stone statues, the moai.

events.title: The Years of Great Disaster
events.body: Dzungar armies invade the Kazakh steppe. Kazakhs remember the flight and famine that follow as the Aqtaban Shubyryndy, the years of barefoot flight.

events.title: Christianity Banned in China
events.body: The Yongzheng Emperor bans Christianity and expels most missionaries, after a long dispute with Rome over Chinese rites.

events.title: The Futa Jallon Jihad
events.body: Around 1725, Fulani Muslims in the highlands of today's Guinea launch a holy war and found an Islamic state — the first of several across West Africa.

events.title: Gulliver's Travels
events.body: Jonathan Swift's satire sends a ship's surgeon to Lilliput, Brobdingnag and stranger places.

events.title: Moulay Ismail Dies
events.body: Morocco's sultan dies after 55 years on the throne. He built the imperial city of Meknes and an army of enslaved Black soldiers; his death brings decades of civil war.

events.title: Dahomey Takes Ouidah
events.body: King Agaja of Dahomey conquers the port of Ouidah. Dahomey becomes one of the great slave-trading states of the coast.

events.title: The Beggar's Opera
events.body: John Gay's 'ballad opera', set among thieves and highwaymen and sung to popular tunes, is the hit of the London season.

events.title: The First Ottoman Press
events.body: Ibrahim Müteferrika prints the first book in Ottoman Turkish using movable type, after permission from the sultan and the religious authorities.

events.title: Portugal Loses Mombasa
events.body: Mombasa's people drive out a Portuguese garrison that had briefly retaken Fort Jesus. Portugal's power on the Swahili coast north of Mozambique is over; Oman's rises.

events.title: The Kazakhs Turn to Russia
events.body: Abu'l-Khayr, khan of the Junior Horde, swears allegiance to the Russian empress, seeking protection from the Dzungars. Russian rule over the steppe follows.

events.title: The St. John Revolt
events.body: Enslaved Akwamu people seize the Danish island of St. John and hold it for six months.

events.title: Sugar on Mauritius
events.body: Governor Mahé de La Bourdonnais builds Port Louis and sugar plantations on French-held Mauritius, worked by enslaved people from Madagascar and East Africa.

events.title: Systema Naturae
events.body: Carl Linnaeus publishes his system for classifying living things. The two-part Latin names he later brings in, like Homo sapiens, are still used.

events.title: Methodism
events.body: At a meeting in Aldersgate Street, John Wesley feels his 'heart strangely warmed'. His preaching to workers and miners in the open air founds Methodism.

events.title: The Maroon Treaty
events.body: After years of war, Britain signs a treaty recognising the freedom and land of Cudjoe's Maroons — people who escaped slavery in Jamaica's mountains.

events.title: Nader Shah Sacks Delhi
events.body: Nader Shah of Iran takes Delhi and orders a massacre in which thousands die. He carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

events.title: The Stono Rebellion
events.body: Enslaved people near Charleston, South Carolina, seize weapons and march south towards Spanish Florida. It is the largest slave revolt in the British mainland colonies.

events.title: Nader Shah Takes Bukhara
events.body: Nader Shah of Iran forces the khanates of Bukhara and Khiva to submit.

events.title: Hasidism
events.body: Around 1740, the Baal Shem Tov begins teaching in Medzhybizh that God can be served through joy and prayer as well as learning. Hasidic Judaism grows from his followers.

events.title: The Batavia Massacre
events.body: Dutch soldiers and townspeople in Batavia kill about 10,000 Chinese residents amid fears of a Chinese uprising.

events.title: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God
events.body: Jonathan Edwards preaches his most famous sermon during the Great Awakening, a wave of revivals across the American colonies.

events.title: Messiah
events.body: Handel's oratorio premieres at a charity concert in Dublin.

events.title: The Pact of Diriyah
events.body: Preacher Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab and local ruler Muhammad bin Saud agree to join religious reform and political power — the foundation of the first Saudi state.

events.title: The First Rules of Golf
events.body: The Gentlemen Golfers of Leith write down thirteen rules for a competition — the oldest surviving rules of golf.

events.title: The Durrani Empire
events.body: After Nader Shah's murder, Ahmad Shah Durrani is chosen leader in Kandahar and founds the state that becomes Afghanistan.

events.title: Pompeii Uncovered
events.body: Excavations begin at Pompeii, the Roman town buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD. Its rediscovered art inspires the neoclassical style across Europe.

events.title: Chūshingura
events.body: The puppet play Kanadehon Chūshingura, retelling the story of the forty-seven rōnin, premieres in Osaka. It becomes one of Japan's best-loved dramas.

events.title: The Atlantic Slave Trade at Its Height
events.body: In the 18th century, European ships carry about six million enslaved Africans across the Atlantic — more than in any other century. Many die on the crossing.

events.title: The Encyclopédie
events.body: Diderot and d'Alembert publish the first volume of a vast encyclopaedia meant to gather all human knowledge and change how people think.

events.title: The Konbaung Dynasty
events.body: A village headman, Alaungpaya, rallies resistance to invaders from the south and founds the dynasty that reunites Burma.

events.title: Franklin's Kite
events.body: Benjamin Franklin flies a kite in a thunderstorm to show that lightning is electricity. His lightning rod follows.

events.title: The Guaraní War
events.body: When Spain and Portugal swap territory, Guaraní people of seven Jesuit missions refuse to move and fight both armies. They are defeated in 1756.

events.title: Johnson's Dictionary
events.body: After nine years' work, Samuel Johnson publishes his dictionary of the English language, with about 40,000 entries.

events.title: The Dzungar Genocide
events.body: Qing armies destroy the Dzungar Khanate. Through war, massacre and smallpox, most of the Dzungar people die; the region becomes part of China as Xinjiang.

events.title: The Lisbon Earthquake
events.body: On All Saints' Day, an earthquake, tsunami and fires destroy most of Lisbon; tens of thousands die. Thinkers across Europe ask how a good God could allow it.

events.title: The Potato Order
events.body: Frederick the Great orders Prussian officials to encourage farmers to grow potatoes. Over the century, the American crop becomes a staple of Europe's poor.

events.title: The Seven Years' War
events.body: Prussia invades Saxony, starting a war fought in Europe, North America, India, West Africa and the Philippines — sometimes called the first world war.

events.title: Plassey
events.body: Robert Clive's East India Company army defeats the Nawab of Bengal, helped by the defection of the Nawab's commander. A trading company becomes a ruling power in India.

events.title: The Canton System
events.body: The Qianlong Emperor limits Western trade to the single port of Canton, under strict rules. Britain's frustration with the system helps lead to the Opium Wars.

events.title: Halley's Comet Returns
events.body: On Christmas night, an amateur astronomer near Dresden spots the comet whose return Edmond Halley had predicted before he died — proof that Newton's laws rule the heavens.

events.title: Candide
events.body: Voltaire's satire mocks the idea that 'all is for the best', sending its hero through war, the Lisbon earthquake and worse.

events.title: The Plains of Abraham
events.body: British troops under James Wolfe defeat the French outside Quebec; both commanders die. New France passes to Britain.

events.title: Tacky's War
events.body: Tacky, an enslaved man from the Gold Coast, leads a rising in Jamaica. It takes British forces more than a year to suppress the revolts that follow.

events.title: The Third Battle of Panipat
events.body: Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghan army crushes the Marathas north of Delhi in one of the largest battles of the century, with tens of thousands killed.

events.title: The Bridgewater Canal
events.body: A canal opens to carry the Duke of Bridgewater's coal to Manchester, halving its price and starting a canal-building boom.

events.title: Harrison's Chronometer
events.body: John Harrison's sea watch H4 sails to Jamaica and keeps time well enough for sailors to find their longitude at sea.

events.title: The Social Contract
events.body: Rousseau publishes his argument that legitimate power comes from the people: 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.'

events.title: The Winter Palace
events.body: Rastrelli completes the Winter Palace in St Petersburg, the main residence of the tsars. It later houses the Hermitage.

events.title: Catherine the Great
events.body: Catherine, a German princess married to Russia's emperor, seizes power in a coup. She rules for 34 years.

events.title: The British Take Havana
events.body: In the Seven Years' War, a British force captures Havana. Spain gets it back the next year in exchange for Florida.

events.title: The British Take Manila
events.body: In the Seven Years' War, a British force captures Manila from Spain and holds it for two years.

events.title: Pontiac's War
events.body: Native nations of the Great Lakes, led in part by the Odawa leader Pontiac, rise against British rule. Britain's proclamation that year limits settlement west of the Appalachians — angering colonists.

events.title: Rio Becomes Brazil's Capital
events.body: Portugal moves the capital of Brazil from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro, the port for the gold fields.

events.title: On Crimes and Punishments
events.body: Cesare Beccaria argues against torture and the death penalty. His short book changes criminal law across Europe and America.

events.title: The Stamp Act
events.body: Parliament taxes paper documents in the American colonies. 'No taxation without representation' becomes the cry; the act is repealed a year later.

events.title: The Company Takes Bengal's Taxes
events.body: The Mughal emperor grants the East India Company the right to collect the revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

events.title: The Jigsaw Puzzle
events.body: Around 1766, London mapmaker John Spilsbury mounts a map on wood and cuts it along the borders — a puzzle to teach geography.

events.title: Ayutthaya Falls
events.body: Burmese armies take and burn Ayutthaya, capital of Siam for four centuries. The general Taksin drives them out and makes a new capital.

events.title: Tahiti
events.body: Samuel Wallis's ship reaches Tahiti. Reports of the island shape European dreams of the South Seas.

events.title: The Jesuits Expelled
events.body: Spain expels the Jesuits from its empire, after Portugal and France. Their missions among the Guaraní and others collapse.

events.title: Ali Bey Defies the Ottomans
events.body: Ali Bey al-Kabir, the Mamluk strongman of Egypt, stops paying tribute to Istanbul and acts as an independent ruler, even invading Syria, until he is overthrown in 1773.

events.title: Nepal Unified
events.body: Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha takes Kathmandu during a festival, uniting the valley kingdoms into Nepal.

events.title: The Transit of Venus
events.body: Astronomers across the world, among them James Cook's expedition on Tahiti, time Venus crossing the Sun to measure the distance from the Earth to the Sun.

events.title: The Era of the Princes
events.body: The murder of Emperor Iyoas begins nearly a century in which regional lords fight over Ethiopia while emperors in Gondar reign without power.

events.title: Cook Reaches Aotearoa
events.body: Cook's Endeavour arrives at Tūranganui-a-Kiwa. Several Māori are killed in the first encounters; the Raiatean navigator Tupaia helps the two sides talk.

events.title: The Boston Massacre
events.body: British soldiers fire into a crowd in Boston, killing five, among them Crispus Attucks, a man of African and Native descent.

events.title: Cook at Botany Bay
events.body: Cook lands at Kamay (Botany Bay). Gweagal men resist the landing. Cook later claims the east coast for Britain.

events.title: The Bengal Famine of 1770
events.body: Drought and Company tax collection bring famine to Bengal. Contemporary estimates said a third of the population died; modern estimates are in the millions.

events.title: The Source of the Blue Nile
events.body: Scottish traveller James Bruce reaches the springs of the Blue Nile in Ethiopia — long known to Ethiopians — after a stay at the imperial court in Gondar.

events.title: The Tây Sơn Rebellion
events.body: Three brothers from Tây Sơn lead a peasant uprising that topples Vietnam's rival ruling houses.

events.title: The Factory
events.body: Richard Arkwright opens a water-powered cotton-spinning mill at Cromford, run in shifts day and night — a model for the factories of the Industrial Revolution.

events.title: The Somerset Case
events.body: An English court frees James Somerset, an enslaved man his owner tried to ship to Jamaica, ruling that he cannot be forced out of England — a judgment widely taken to mean English law gives slavery no support.

events.title: The First Partition of Poland
events.body: Russia, Prussia and Austria each take a slice of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

events.title: The Santa Marta Earthquakes
events.body: Earthquakes wreck Santiago de Guatemala, the colonial capital. The government moves to a new city, today's Guatemala City; the ruins become Antigua.

events.title: Phillis Wheatley
events.body: Phillis Wheatley, taken from West Africa as a child and enslaved in Boston, publishes a book of poems in London — the first book of poetry by an African American.

events.title: Pugachev's Rebellion
events.body: Cossack Yemelyan Pugachev, claiming to be the murdered Tsar Peter III, leads serfs, Cossacks and Bashkirs in Russia's largest peasant revolt.

events.title: The Boston Tea Party
events.body: Protesters disguised as Mohawk men dump 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbour.

events.title: The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
events.body: After defeat by Russia, the Ottomans give up control of the Crimean Khanate and accept Russia as a protector of Orthodox Christians in their empire.

events.title: The Sorrows of Young Werther
events.body: Goethe's novel of a young man's hopeless love becomes a craze across Europe — with young men copying Werther's yellow waistcoat and blue coat.

events.title: Lexington and Concord
events.body: Colonial militia exchange fire with British troops — 'the shot heard round the world'. The American Revolutionary War begins.

sources.title: April 19, 1775
sources.publisher: US National Park Service — Minute Man

events.title: Thomas Paine Publishes Common Sense
events.body: Paine's 47-page pamphlet argues for American independence in plain language accessible to ordinary readers. It sells approximately 100,000 copies in three months — the best-selling printed work per capita in American history — and transforms the political imagination of the colonies.

events.title: Gibbon: Decline and Fall of Rome Vol. I
events.body: Gibbon publishes the first volume of his magisterial history, tracing Rome from its height through the fall of Constantinople in 1453. Its sceptical treatment of Christianity shocks contemporaries; its prose and scope remain unmatched in English historical writing.

events.title: Adam Smith Publishes The Wealth of Nations
events.body: Smith publishes the foundational text of modern economics, arguing for free markets, the division of labour, and the 'invisible hand.' It provides the intellectual framework for industrial capitalism and remains the most influential work of economics ever written.

events.title: British Forces Evacuate Boston
events.body: After an 11-month siege, British forces evacuate Boston following Washington's fortification of Dorchester Heights with cannon from Fort Ticonderoga. The first significant American military success of the Revolutionary War shifts the war's focus southward.

events.title: The Illuminati Founded in Bavaria
events.body: Adam Weishaupt founds the Order of the Illuminati, advocating Enlightenment values including rationalism and separation of Church and State. Suppressed by the Bavarian government in 1785, its brief existence generates conspiracy theories that persist into the 21st century.

events.title: Watt's Steam Engine Gains Commercial Traction
events.body: Watt and Boulton's improved steam engine — with its separate condenser — begins transforming industry. Within a generation it powers cotton mills, iron foundries, and railways. It is the engine of the Industrial Revolution.

events.title: United States Declaration of Independence
events.body: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence, drafted primarily by Thomas Jefferson. It declares thirteen colonies free states, articulating natural rights and popular sovereignty. It remains one of the most influential political documents in history.
events.imageCredit: National Archives of the United States / Wikimedia Commons

events.title: The Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
events.body: Spain creates a new viceroyalty ruled from Buenos Aires, covering today's Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia.

events.title: Battle of Long Island
events.body: British forces decisively defeat Washington's Continental Army in the largest battle of the Revolution by troop numbers. Washington loses approximately 1,500 men but saves his army through a daring overnight retreat across the East River under cover of fog.

events.title: Nathan Hale Executed as a Spy
events.body: Nathan Hale, a 21-year-old schoolteacher and Continental Army captain, is executed by the British after being captured behind enemy lines. He reportedly said: 'I only regret that I have but one life to lose for my country.'

events.title: Washington Crosses the Delaware
events.body: Washington leads a daring overnight crossing of the ice-choked Delaware River on Christmas night, launching a surprise attack on Hessian forces at Trenton. The victory — at a cost of two American deaths from exposure — revives collapsing Revolutionary morale.

events.title: Saratoga
events.body: A British army surrenders at Saratoga. France, convinced the Americans can win, enters the war on their side.

events.title: Cook Killed in Hawaii
events.body: James Cook is killed at Kealakekua Bay in a clash with Hawaiians after he tries to take their chief hostage.

events.title: The First Frontier War
events.body: Xhosa and colonial farmers clash along the Fish River — the first of nine frontier wars over land and cattle that last a century.

events.title: The Great Hurricane of 1780
events.body: The deadliest Atlantic hurricane on record strikes Barbados, Martinique and St Eustatius, killing more than 20,000 people.

events.title: The Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II
events.body: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, descended from the last Inca, takes the name Túpac Amaru II and leads a vast Andean uprising against Spanish abuses. He and his wife Micaela Bastidas are executed in Cusco in 1781.

events.title: Uranus Discovered
events.body: Musician and amateur astronomer William Herschel spots a new planet from his garden in Bath — the first discovered with a telescope.

events.title: Critique of Pure Reason
events.body: Immanuel Kant asks what human reason can know at all. The book reshapes philosophy.

events.title: Yorktown
events.body: Trapped by American and French armies and a French fleet, Lord Cornwallis surrenders. The war is effectively over.

events.title: Bangkok Founded
events.body: Rama I founds the Chakri dynasty, which still reigns, and moves the capital across the river to Bangkok.

events.title: Russia Annexes Crimea, 1783
events.body: Catherine the Great annexes the Crimean Khanate. Many Crimean Tatars leave for Ottoman lands.

events.title: The Queen in a Chemise
events.body: Vigée Le Brun's portrait of Marie Antoinette in a simple muslin dress scandalises the Paris Salon and is taken down — but the loose white dress soon sweeps Europe.

events.title: The Treaty of Paris
events.body: Britain recognises the independence of the United States.

events.title: The First Balloon Flight
events.body: Two men rise over Paris in a hot-air balloon made by the Montgolfier brothers — the first people to fly.

events.title: The Asiatic Society
events.body: William Jones founds a society in Calcutta for the study of Asia. Two years later he points out that Sanskrit, Greek and Latin share a common ancestor.

events.title: The Marriage of Figaro
events.body: Beaumarchais's comedy, in which a clever servant outwits his noble master, opens in Paris after years of censorship.

events.title: Deep Time
events.body: James Hutton tells the Royal Society of Edinburgh that the Earth's rocks were formed by slow processes still at work — over a vastly longer time than anyone had imagined.

events.title: Mozart's Figaro
events.body: Mozart's opera of Beaumarchais's play premieres in Vienna.

events.title: The Abolition Committee
events.body: Twelve men, mostly Quakers, meet in London to campaign against the slave trade. Josiah Wedgwood's medallion of a kneeling man in chains, 'Am I Not a Man and a Brother?', becomes their emblem.

events.title: Andrianampoinimerina
events.body: Around 1787, Andrianampoinimerina takes power in Imerina and begins uniting the highlands of Madagascar around Antananarivo.

events.title: The US Constitution
events.body: Delegates in Philadelphia sign a constitution for the United States. It counts an enslaved person as three-fifths of a person for representation.

events.title: The First Fleet
events.body: Eleven British ships land about 1,400 people — more than half of them convicts — at Sydney Cove to found a penal colony on Gadigal land. 26 January is still argued over as Australia Day.

sources.title: First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove
sources.publisher: National Museum of Australia — Defining Moments

events.title: The Interesting Narrative
events.body: Olaudah Equiano publishes the story of his capture as a child, the Middle Passage, slavery and freedom. It becomes a key book of the abolition campaign.

events.title: Smallpox in Sydney
events.body: Smallpox breaks out among the Aboriginal people around Sydney Harbour and kills a large part of them. How it arrived is still debated.

events.title: Mutiny on the Bounty
events.body: Near Tonga, crew of HMS Bounty set Captain Bligh and loyal men adrift. Bligh sails 6,700 kilometres to Timor; the mutineers settle on Pitcairn.

events.title: Modern Chemistry
events.body: Antoine Lavoisier publishes the first modern list of chemical elements and shows that matter is conserved in reactions. He is guillotined in 1794.

events.title: The Storming of the Bastille
events.body: Crowds in Paris storm the royal prison-fortress for its gunpowder. The French Revolution begins.

events.title: The Rights of Man
events.body: France's National Assembly declares that 'men are born and remain free and equal in rights'.

sources.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man, 1789

events.title: Washington's Thanksgiving Proclamation
events.body: President Washington declares Thursday 26 November 'a day of public thanksgiving and prayer' for the new nation and its constitution.

events.title: The Women's March on Versailles
events.body: Thousands of market women, angry at the price of bread, march to Versailles and bring the royal family back to Paris.

events.title: Pemulwuy's War
events.body: Pemulwuy, a Bidjigal man, spears the governor's gamekeeper, beginning twelve years of resistance to the colony.

events.title: The Aztec Sun Stone
events.body: Workers paving Mexico City's main square uncover a huge carved Aztec stone, months after finding the statue of the goddess Coatlicue.

events.title: Dream of the Red Chamber
events.body: Cao Xueqin's novel of the rise and fall of a great family, circulated in manuscript for decades, is printed for the first time. It is often called China's greatest novel.

events.title: The Haitian Revolution Begins
events.body: Enslaved people in the north of Saint-Domingue, France's richest colony, rise up after a ceremony at Bois Caïman. Toussaint Louverture soon emerges as their leader.

events.title: The Rights of Woman
events.body: Playwright Olympe de Gouges answers the Rights of Man with a declaration of the rights of women. She is guillotined in 1793.

events.title: The Bill of Rights
events.body: The first ten amendments to the US Constitution, protecting free speech, religion, the press and fair trials, come into force.

events.title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
events.body: Mary Wollstonecraft argues that women seem less rational than men only because they are denied education.

events.title: Freetown Founded
events.body: About 1,200 Black Loyalists — people who escaped slavery by fighting for Britain in the American war — sail from Nova Scotia and found Freetown.

events.title: Tiradentes Hanged
events.body: Tiradentes, a leader of a plot for Brazilian independence in Minas Gerais, is hanged and quartered in Rio. Brazil now marks the day as a national holiday.

events.title: Louis XVI Executed
events.body: The former king of France is guillotined in Paris.

events.title: The Permanent Settlement
events.body: The British fix Bengal's land tax for ever, making zamindars landowners responsible for it. Peasants lose their old rights.

events.title: The Cotton Gin
events.body: Eli Whitney's machine separates cotton fibre from its seeds far faster than by hand. Cotton growing — and slavery — spread across the American South.

events.title: The Louvre Opens
events.body: The royal palace of the Louvre opens to the public as a museum of art belonging to the nation.

events.title: The Macartney Embassy
events.body: Britain's envoy meets the Qianlong Emperor to ask for open trade and a permanent embassy. The emperor refuses, saying China has no need of British goods.

events.title: The Terror
events.body: The revolutionary government under Robespierre declares terror 'the order of the day'. About 17,000 people are officially executed before Robespierre himself falls in July 1794.

events.title: France Abolishes Slavery
events.body: Revolutionary France abolishes slavery in all its colonies. Napoleon restores it in 1802.

events.title: The Graaff-Reinet Republic
events.body: Frontier farmers drive out the Company's magistrate and declare their own republic, angry over taxes and frontier policy.

events.title: The Battle of Nuʻuanu
events.body: Kamehameha's army conquers Oʻahu, driving its defenders over the cliffs of the Nuʻuanu Pali.

events.title: The British Take the Cape
events.body: After the battle of Muizenberg, the Dutch East India Company hands the Cape to Britain to keep it from revolutionary France. It is returned in 1803 — and taken again in 1806.

events.title: Poland Wiped Off the Map
events.body: In the third partition, Russia, Prussia and Austria divide what is left of Poland. It does not exist as a state again until 1918.

events.title: The Smallpox Vaccine
events.body: Edward Jenner infects a boy with cowpox and then shows he is immune to smallpox — the first vaccine.

events.title: The White Lotus Rebellion
events.body: A rebellion led by a Buddhist sect breaks out in central China over taxes and hardship. It takes the Qing nearly a decade and huge sums to put down.

events.title: Hwaseong Fortress
events.body: King Jeongjo of Korea completes a new fortress city at Suwon, built with cranes and pulleys from a scholar's designs.

events.title: Mungo Park Reaches the Niger
events.body: Scottish explorer Mungo Park sees the Niger at Ségou and finds that it flows east, not west.

events.title: Missionaries Reach Tahiti
events.body: The ship Duff lands the first Protestant missionaries of the London Missionary Society on Tahiti.

events.title: The Creation
events.body: Haydn's oratorio of the creation of the world, from chaos to Adam and Eve, is first performed in Vienna.

events.title: The Irish Rebellion of 1798
events.body: The United Irishmen, inspired by the French Revolution, rise against British rule. The rising is crushed and thousands are killed.

events.title: Malthus on Population
events.body: Thomas Malthus argues that population always grows faster than food, so poverty can never be ended. Forty years later, reading Malthus helps lead Darwin to natural selection.

events.title: Napoleon in Egypt
events.body: Napoleon defeats the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids and takes Cairo. Days later Nelson destroys his fleet at the Nile. French scholars who came with him survey Egypt's monuments.

sources.title: The Institut d’Égypte and the Description de l’Égypte
Description de l’Égypte: the book that tried to capture a civilisation

events.title: Lyrical Ballads
events.body: Wordsworth and Coleridge publish poems in everyday language about ordinary lives, including 'The Rime of the Ancient Mariner' — the start of English Romanticism.

events.title: Tipu Sultan Falls
events.body: Tipu Sultan of Mysore, who fought the British with rockets and French help, is killed defending his capital. The Company dominates southern India.

events.title: Ranjit Singh Takes Lahore
events.body: Eighteen-year-old Ranjit Singh takes Lahore, the start of his Sikh empire.

events.title: The Rosetta Stone
events.body: French soldiers rebuilding a fort near Rashid find a stone carved with the same decree in hieroglyphs, demotic and Greek — the key to reading ancient Egyptian.

events.title: Humboldt in the Americas
events.body: Alexander von Humboldt lands at Cumaná, Venezuela, beginning five years of travel through Spanish America that change how science sees nature.

events.title: Napoleon Seizes Power
events.body: In the coup of 18 Brumaire, General Napoleon Bonaparte overthrows the government and makes himself First Consul.

events.title: The Dutch East India Company Dissolved
events.body: Bankrupt, the Dutch East India Company is dissolved. Its territories in the East Indies pass to the Dutch state.
